findings.reason: the rule needs an explicit clause for an undeclared window (unbounded ranks above any declared one); as written it does not yield the outcome the same section asserts, so the node returns a red gate and the rule must be restated.
findings.text: §15's deliverable picks "the one with the largest usable input window, ties broken by backend name", but only `clive` declares `usable_input_window` (host `flight.yaml:423`); codex declares none, and `routing.py:3449-3450` treats an absent window as *unbounded*, returning no window figure at all. So the comparator's key does not exist for the very lane the section says it will choose (".on this host it chooses codex over local"), and the natural implementation — `max(fitting, key=...get("usable_input_window") or 0)` — ranks the unbounded lane last and can select a different backend, contradicting the section's own first arm

findings.reason: naming the enumeration is one clause and removes a second fit implementation plus its per-lane subprocess cost on the fallback path.
findings.text: the deliverable says the fallback "applies the same context-fit check the router's `_fit` applies" and then chooses "among the backends that fit", but it never names what enumerates those backends. The only route that produces fit-checked candidates is `picker.snapshot.candidates` (which §5 names and which runs `_fit` per backend under the lifts in force); a node told only "the backends that fit" will hand-roll a loop over `config["backends"]`, re-deriving competence per backend — a git subprocess per lane on the dispatch path this section exists to keep cheap, and a second implementation of a check the section says it reuses

findings.reason: splitting the arm into two cases and adding a control that removes the job read is a one-line done-when change, and without it the clause this edit added is the one clause the gate cannot measure.
findings.text: §6's third arm reads "A waiting run whose probe value is still moving, or whose named external job is alive, stays waiting": one case covering a disjunction, so a fixture whose probe value moves satisfies the arm with the scheduler-jobs clause absent, and the stated negative control ("removes the liveness clause, and the second arm fails") removes the process-liveness clause, which cannot red the job clause either. The section's newest mechanism — the `squeue -h -j <id>` read that exists precisely because a scheduler-backed wait legitimately has no process — therefore ships with no arm and no control that can fail on its removal

findings.reason: the mechanism and the shortfall are unaffected; the corrected range (12:05-18:49Z with two gated passes) even strengthens the case, and no node's behaviour turns on the wording.
findings.text: §15 says the request was "refused ... on every pass from 13:08 to 18:49Z"; the cited log's own rows for `r-20261028T112435754554-csrr-fdu-idm-stray-per-circuit` begin at 12:05:33Z and include two passes inside the stated interval (16:05:20Z and 16:16:37Z) recorded `held-by-gate`, not `refused`. The token figures the section quotes are exact (236783 against 230144, 24 rows), so the evidence is sound; only the quoted interval is not
